rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose clause describes the polytheists’ aim in tempting the Prophet: they hoped he would invent something besides what was revealed; it says nothing about his own intention.
rows.anchor: متعلق ب { يفتنونك } ، واللام للعلة ، أي يفعلون ذلك إضمارا منهم وطمعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose-lām concerns the doers’ aim alone and does not imply that the person acted upon shared that aim or knew of it.
rows.anchor: لام التعليل لا تقتضي أكثر من غرض فاعل الفعل المعلل ولا تقتضي غرض المفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here إن is the lightened form of the emphatic إن, with an omitted pronoun of شأن; the lām in ليفتنونك distinguishes it from negative إن and adds no emphasis.
rows.anchor: مخففة من ( إن ) المشددة واسمها ضمير شأن محذوف ، واللام في { ليفتنونك } هي اللام الفارقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about taking the Prophet as a close friend is coordinated with the tempting clause; إذا is a conditional particle whose nūn belongs to the word, and the result is tied to their tempting him.
rows.anchor: وإذا لاتخذوك خليلا } عطف على جملة { وإن كادوا ليفتنونك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inserted إذا with the coordinating و gives the coordination the sense of a consequential فاء; the coordination also suits this as one of the states in which they pressed the Prophet.
rows.anchor: مقحما بين المتعاطفين لتصير واو العطف مع ( إذا ) مفيدة معنى فاء التفريع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The implied condition is that, had they turned him from some revelation, they would have taken him as a close friend; the lām in لاتخذوك is the oath-prefacing lām and the response lām to لو.
rows.anchor: والتقدير : فلو صرفوك عن بعض ما أوحينا إليك لاتخذوك خليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خليل means a friend.
rows.anchor: والخليل : الصديق . وتقدم عند قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary links the word خليل to its earlier occurrence in the account of Abraham.
rows.anchor: واتخذ الله إبراهيم خليلا في سورة النساء ( 125 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He allows the passage to be an independent statement of another divine favor and circumstance for the Prophet, or a continuation in which the inclination concerns what the earlier reports say the polytheists requested.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون هذا كلاما مستقلا غير متصل بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لولا denotes that its result is prevented because its condition exists.
rows.anchor: أي يقتضي امتناع جوابه لوجود شرطه ، أي بسبب وجود شرطه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تثبيت literally means making something fixed; figuratively it means keeping the Prophet unchanged in his course.
rows.anchor: والتثبيت : جعل الشيء ثابتا ، أي متمكنا من مكانه غير مقلقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun for the Prophet’s person stands for his understanding and judgment: God kept his view steady in dealing with the polytheists.
rows.anchor: والمراد تثبيت فهمه ورأيه ، وهذا من الحكم على الذات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the first reading of the passage, inclination is a general possibility that is wholly prevented by divine protection, just as the attempted temptation itself was prevented.
rows.anchor: أن الركون مجمل في أشياء هي مظنة الركون ولكن الركون منتف من أصله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the continuation reading, God protected the Prophet from mistaken judgment and showed that firmness in religion and honoring its weak followers outweighed appeasing powerful polytheists.
rows.anchor: ولولا أن عصمناك من الخطأ في الاجتهاد وأريناك أن مصلحة الشدة في الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Concessions over religious matters would invite the polytheists to make increasingly far-reaching demands; firm resolve therefore outweighed conciliation.
rows.anchor: فإن إظهار الهوادة في أمر الدين تطمع المشركين في الترقي إلى سؤال ما هو أبعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypothetical slight inclination would have followed from mistaking an apparent, lesser benefit—their promised faith—for the greater but less obvious benefit of holding firm; it did not occur.
rows.anchor: استنادا لدليل مصلحة مرجوحة واضحة وغفلة عن مصلحة راجحة خفية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ركون derives from leaning with one’s side and, by proximity, denotes agreement; the commentary links its use to the prohibition on leaning toward wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: والركون : الميل بالركن ، أي بالجانب من الجسد واستعمل في الموافقة بعلاقة القرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression about turning one’s side away in 17:83 is the contrary image to ركون.
rows.anchor: كما استعمل ضده في المخالفة في قوله تعالى : وإذا أنعمنا على الإنسان أعرض ونأى بجانبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: شيئا is an absolute object meaning some inclination; the indefinite noun and قليلا both reduce the amount, while شيئا also avoids the heavier verbal noun الركون.
rows.anchor: وانتصب شيئا } على المفعول المطلق ل { تركن } ، أي شيئا من الركون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite شيء often conveys minimization because it leaves the kind unspecified; he cites the prohibition on taking anything from a wife’s dowry as an example.
rows.anchor: فإن كلمة ( شيء ) لتوغلها في إبهام جنس ما تضاف إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second إذن is the conditional consequence of كدت تركن, so it is not coordinated with a conjunction.
rows.anchor: و ( إذن ) الثانية جزاء ل كدت تركن } ، ولكونها جزاء فصلت عن العطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse emphatically rules out both actual inclination and approaching it through four restraints: لولا, the verb of near occurrence, شيئا, and قليلا; قد is nullified within the impossible condition.
rows.anchor: لأن الآية قد نفته بأربعة أمور ، وهي : ( لولا ) الامتناعية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional إذن introduces the consequence: if the Prophet had inclined to them, God would have made him taste a doubled punishment in life and at death.
rows.anchor: وجملة { إذا لأذقناك ضعف الحياة } جزاء لجملة { لقد كدت تركن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The doubled punishment is not literal because no amount of punishment is specified to be doubled.
rows.anchor: إذ ليس ثم علم بمقدار العذاب يراد تضعيفه كقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here ضعف is not literal doubling against a known measure; it describes punishment as severe, as in the cited expression of a doubled fire-punishment.
rows.anchor: ثم إن الضعف أطلق هنا على القوي الشديد لعدم حمل الضعف على حقيقته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The genitive construction means punishment in life and in death: worldly calamities would accumulate, destroying the joy of a completed mission and leaving the Prophet subdued among enemies.
rows.anchor: وإضافة الضعف إلى الحياة وإلى الممات على معنى ( في )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ضعف الممات may mean that the punishment of life continues until death.
rows.anchor: ويشبه أن يكون قوله : وضعف الممات } في استمرار ضعف الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ضعف الممات does not mean punishment in the afterlife: a slight inclination from religious judgment for perceived benefit would not merit otherworldly punishment, since prophets may exercise judgment and a mistaken jurist is rewarded.
rows.anchor: فليس المراد من ضعف الممات عذاب الآخرة لأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لو ركن إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good intentions do not avert worldly hardship caused by a mistaken course; the wording therefore departs from the usual expression for afterlife punishment.
rows.anchor: وأما مصائب الدنيا وأرزاؤها فهي مسببة على أسباب من الأغلاط والأخطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ثم ranks the inability to escape the punishment above the punishment itself; نصير can mean a rescuer from defeat or one who avenges the defeated.
rows.anchor: و ( ثم ) للترتيب الرتبي لأن عدم الخلاص من العذاب أهم من إذاقته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ليخرجوك gives the purpose of the intimidation: they sought to make the Prophet leave the land for good, a narrower outcome than intimidation itself.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { ليخرجوك } تعليل للاستفزاز ، أي استفزازا لقصد الإخراج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause that they would not remain after him may be coordinated with the preceding clause or parenthetical; on the latter reading, إذا is a time adverb attached to يلبثون.
rows.anchor: عطف على جملة { وإن كادوا } ، أو هي اعتراض في آخر الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After a conjunction, the conditional إذا construction permits either a subjunctive imperfect with implicit أن or an indicative imperfect.
rows.anchor: فإذا وقعت بعد عاطف جاز رفع المضارع بعدها ونصبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third analysis makes إذا a time adverb with an omitted clause, as some Kufan grammarians propose; this is plausible because after conjunctions the subjunctive is rare and a conditional result is not apparent.
rows.anchor: وتنوينها عوض عن جملة محذوفة على قول جماعة من نحاة الكوفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The implied time clause is: when they expel you, or when you leave, they will remain only briefly behind you.
rows.anchor: والتقدير : وإذا أخرجوك أو وإذا خرجت لا يلبثون خلفك إلا قليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers read خلفك; it means after you, extending the original sense of behind to temporal succession.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { خلفك } . و { خلفك } أريد به بعدك

rows.speaker: ابن عامر، وحمزة، والكسائي، وحفص، وخلف
rows.claim: These readers have خلافك, a dialectal equivalent of خلفك.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر ، وحمزة ، والكسائي ، وحفص ، وخلف { خلافك } وهو لغة في خلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لبث means settling in a place; the Meccans who caused the emigration soon left for Badr and died there, while God preserved most of them to enter Islam later.
rows.anchor: واللبث : الاستقرار في المكان ، أي لا يستقرون في مكة بل يخرجون منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage intimates both that the Messenger will leave Mecca and that those who cause his departure will remain there only briefly.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية إيماء إلى أن الرسول سيخرج من مكة وأن مخرجيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سنة means an established custom or course; God's settled practice was that a people who drove out a messenger would not remain after him, as illustrated by the peoples of Hud, Salih, Abraham, and Lot.
rows.anchor: والسنة : العادة والسيرة التي يلتزمها صاحبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سنة is accusative as an absolute object if it is a verbal noun, or circumstantial if it is a lexical noun; its construction connects it to those sent earlier.
rows.anchor: وانتصب { سنة } من { من قد أرسلنا } على المفعولية المطلقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explanatory sentence says why their stay would be brief: conspiracies to expel messengers lead God to command migration so they do not remain humiliated among their people, like the Arab practice of khulʿ.
rows.anchor: وإنما سن الله هذه السنة لرسله لأن تآمر الأقوام على إخراجهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that God’s practice cannot be changed is parenthetical completion; لا تجد intensifies the denial, and تحويل means changing or replacing a state.
rows.anchor: وجملة { ولا تجد لسنتنا تحويلا } اعتراض لتكملة البيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects as false the unusual report that Jews sent the Prophet to Syria, prompting the Tabuk expedition and this revelation; the known history of Tabuk contradicts it, though some use it to date the verse as Medinan.
rows.anchor: ومن غريب التفسير أن المراد : أن اليهود قالوا للنبيء الحق بأرض الشام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The five daily prayers were prescribed on the Night Journey by a sound hadith, but this schedule later clarified prayer times after the obligation had been established and communicated to the Companions.
rows.anchor: كان شرع الصلوات الخمس للأمة ليلة الإسراء ، كما ثبت في الحديث الصحيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse gathers the prayer legislation given around the Night Journey and begins a fresh passage.
rows.anchor: فلذلك جاءت هذه الآية في هذه السورة التي نزلت عقب حادث الإسراء جمعا للتشريع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After granting protection and victory, God commands gratitude through prayer and additional worship, which prepares for the promised praised station.
rows.anchor: أن الله لما امتن على النبي بالعصمة وبالنصر ذكره بشكر النعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though the command addresses the Prophet, Quranic legislative address to him normally includes his community unless evidence indicates exclusive application; Muslims understood this convention.
rows.anchor: أن خطاب النبي بتشريعع تدخل فيه أمته إلا إذا دل دليل على اختصاصه بذلك الحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إقامة prayer is figurative for persistent, regular observance; لام in لدلوك marks timing and means عند.
rows.anchor: والإقامة : مجاز في المواظبة والإدامة . وقد تقدم عند قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: دلوك has three attested senses: the sun’s passage from its midday zenith, its later movement toward the afternoon, or its setting, making it a shared term.
rows.anchor: فصار لفظ الدلوك مشتركا في المعاني الثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: غسق is darkness at the disappearance of the twilight glow, the time of the evening prayer, also called العتمة.
rows.anchor: والغسق : الظلمة ، وهي انقطاع بقايا شعاع الشمس حين يماثل سواد أفق الغروب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night-prayer command is coordinated with Qur'an at dawn, which is itself an implied clause governed by the command to establish prayer.
rows.anchor: عطف على { وقرآن الفجر ( الإسراء : 78 ) فإنه في تقدير جملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Advancing the phrase ومن الليل gives it emphasis and encouragement, and its position before the verb creates a conditional-result flavor marked by فاء.
rows.anchor: وقدم المجرور المتعلق ب تهجد على متعلقه اهتماما به وتحريضا عليه

rows.speaker: الزجاج والزمخشري
rows.claim: They take ومن الليل as an exhortation meaning some of the night, on the assumption that Qur'an at dawn is also an exhortation; Ibn Ashur calls this a sound alternative.
rows.anchor: وجعل الزجاج والزمخشري قوله : ومن الليل } في معنى الإغراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun به refers to the Qur'an mentioned as Qur'an at dawn, but here to Qur'an generally, like saying “I have a dirham and half of it.”
rows.anchor: وضمير به } للقرآن المذكور في قوله : { وقرآن الفجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ indicates means or cause; tahajjud is prayer during the night, derived from sleep with a form that denotes removing sleep.
rows.anchor: والتهجد : الصلاة في أثناء الليل ، وهو اسم مشتق من الهجود ، وهو النوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نافلة is an additional beloved act; لك marks its special obligation for the Prophet, while it remains encouraged for others and is linked to the command in al-Muzzammil.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا دليل على أن الأمر بالتهجد خاص بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فالأمر للوجوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The obligation of night prayer specially honors the Prophet, and the promise of the praised station explains why it is imposed on him; a divine expression of hope is a promise.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا الإيجاب عليه زيادة تشريف له ، ولهذا أعقب بوعد أن يبعثه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مقام is a place for standing, here a place appointed for a great event; it is the adverbial setting of يبعثك.
rows.anchor: والمقام : محل القيام . والمراد به المكان المعدود لأمر عظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the station praised is figurative: its occupant is praised because of his effect there, namely the supreme intercession.
rows.anchor: ووصف المقام بالمحمود وصف مجازي . والمحمود من يقوم فيه

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar reports that humanity gathers in groups following their prophets and asks each to intercede until the request reaches Muhammad; this is the praised station.
rows.anchor: وفي ( صحيح البخاري ) عن ابن عمر ( أن الناس يصيرون يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet identifying the praised station as intercession; al-Tirmidhi grades the report hasan sahih.
rows.anchor: وفي ( جامع الترمذي ) عن أبي هريرة قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Bukhari gives a detailed account of the intercession, a station for which everyone at the gathering will praise the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وذلك مقام يحمده فيه كل أهل المحشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After bodily gratitude through prayer, the Prophet is taught verbal gratitude: ask God for a sound departure and arrival, so enemies’ expulsion will not harm him; the prayer also fits the praised station.
rows.anchor: لما أمره الله تعالى بالشكر الفعلي عطف عليه الأمر بالشكر اللساني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer hints that God will move him from Mecca to a place of migration; the verse appears to have been revealed shortly before the First Aqaba pledge.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا التلقين إشارة إلهية إلى أن الله تعالى مخرجه من مكة إلى مهاجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forms مدخل and مخرج denote places of entry and exit, chosen to ask for transitions made easy by God; the prayer encompasses every literal or figurative passage.
rows.anchor: اختير هنا الاسم المشتق من الفعل المتعدي للإشارة إلى أن المطلوب دخول وخروج ميسران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: صدق means completeness and excellence in its kind: a good, praiseworthy entry or exit.
rows.anchor: والصدق : هنا الكمال وما يحمد في نوعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer for a helpful authority also asks for support in those transitions and across distant lands, work, followers, and enemies.
rows.anchor: وعطف عليه سؤال التأييد والنصر في تلك المداخل والمخارج وغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سلطان can mean power, proof, or kingship; the word gathers all three, which God granted through victory, persuasive evidence, fear in enemies, and rule.
rows.anchor: فالسلطان : اسم مصدر يطلق على السلطة وعلى الحجة وعلى الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the taught prayer for right action and support, the Prophet is taught an announcement phrased as a past event, signaling that the promised answer and victory have arrived.
rows.anchor: أعقب تلقينه الدعاء بسداد أعماله وتأييده فيها بأن لقنه هذا الإعلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the Messenger’s mission establishes truth and abolishes falsehood, the declaration promises his triumph; at the conquest of Mecca he recited it in the Kaaba as the idols fell.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت دعوة الرسول هي لإقامة الحق وإبطالل الباطل كان الوعد بظهور الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Truth’s coming figuratively means people recognizing and practicing it, and its proponents prevailing; falsehood’s departure means its adherents abandoning it.
rows.anchor: ومجيء الحق مستعمل مجازا في إدراك الناس إياه وعملهم به وانتصار القائم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: زهق means perishing after existence; the statement means that the Prophet’s truth became established and spread while the falsehood he opposed ended.
rows.anchor: و { زهق } اضمحل بعد وجوده . ومصدره الزهوق والزهق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final clause is a generalizing conclusion: falsehood never lasts, so truth, its opposite, remains and prevails across communities and eras.
rows.anchor: وجملة { إن الباطل كان زهوقا } تذييل للجملة التي قبله لما فيه من عموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كان marks perishing as falsehood’s enduring pattern in every age; he links this to the opening of Yunus.
rows.anchor: ودل فعل { كان } على أن الزهوق شنشنة الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This continues the support and threat begun at 17:73: the Qur'an that opponents wanted altered keeps descending, healing the Messenger and believers while increasing unjust opponents’ loss.
rows.anchor: فإنه بعد أن امتن عليه بأن أيده بالعصمة من الركون إليهم وتبشيره بالنصرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an angers those who wanted the Prophet to replace it with one that did not criticize their idols; it is the source of truth and refutation of falsehood.
rows.anchor: وهو القرآن الذي طمعوا أن يسألوا النبي أن يبدله بقرآن ليس فيه ذكر أصنامهم بسوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperfect form of the intensified verb of sending signifies renewed, repeated, abundant revelation and promises its continuation for a long time.
rows.anchor: اختير للإخبار عن التنزيل الفعل المضارع المشتق من فعل المضاعف للدلالة على التجديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما is the object of ننزل, while من القرآن explains its otherwise indefinite reference; من is neither partitive nor an origin marker.
rows.anchor: وليست ( من ) للتبعيض ولا للابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Healing literally removes illness and figuratively removes false beliefs, corrupt actions, blameworthy traits, and barriers to benefit; the commentary begins a poetic illustration by Antara.
rows.anchor: والشفاء حقيقته زوال الداء ، ويستعمل مجازا في زوال ما هو نقص وضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جانب means flank or side; the bāʾ marks accompaniment, and moving one’s side away depicts recoil from something.
rows.anchor: والجانب : الجنب . وهو الجهة من الجسد التي فيها اليد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase نأى بجانبه adds distancing and recoil beyond the meaning of أعرض; the rejected person turns away from worship and gratitude.
rows.anchor: فالمفاد من قوله : { وناء بجانبه } صد عن العبادة والشكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of turning away is omitted because context supplies it: the person turns away from God, worship, commands, and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: وحذف متعلق { أعرض ونأى } لدلالة المقام عليه

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read وناء with hamza after nūn and alif after the hamza.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { وناء } بهمزة بعد النون وألف بعد الهمزة

rows.speaker: ابن ذكوان، أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Ibn Amir in Ibn Dhakwan’s transmission and Abu Jaafar read the letters in reversed order; this metathesis eases a hamza after a consonant followed by a long vowel.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر في رواية ابن ذكوان وأبو جعفر { وناء } بألف بعد النون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative explanation takes ناء in that reading to mean becoming heavy with respect to gratitude, as in the parable of one who clings to the earth.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ناء في هذه القراءة بمعنى ثقل ، أي عن الشكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The distress clause prevents the inference that losing blessings reforms the person: in hardship he despairs, remains angry and constricted, and does not repent; this does not conflict with 41:51.
rows.anchor: وجملة وإذا مسه الشر كان يؤسا احتراس من أن يتوهم السامع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يؤسا is an intensive form, and كان conveys entrenched despair; the response is striking because hardship should prompt reflection on ways to remedy it.
rows.anchor: ودل قوله : كان يؤسا } على قوة يأسه إذ صيغ له مثال المبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surrounding pronouns point to Quraysh as the questioners; a Tirmidhi report from Ibn Abbas says they asked Jews for a question, were told to ask about the spirit, and this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: وقد روى الترمذي عن ابن عباس قال : قالت قريش ليهود أعطونا شيئا نسأل هذا الرجل عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Ibn Abbas’s account they asked about the spirit alone and the verse was revealed for that question, so its placement among other material poses no problem; its timing may reflect a separate revelation.
rows.anchor: وظاهر هذا أنهم سألوه عن الروح خاصة وأن الآية نزلت بسبب سؤالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mecca and Yathrib had extensive marriage, trade, and personal ties; people from each town lodged with local friends, as with Umayya ibn Khalaf and Saʿd ibn Muʿadh.
rows.anchor: وكان لكل يثربي صاحب بمكة ينزل عنده إذا قدم الآخر بلده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Quraysh sent al-Nadr ibn al-Harith and ʿUqba ibn Abi Muʿayṭ to Jewish scholars, who proposed questions about the Cave, Dhul-Qarnayn, and the spirit; the first two were answered in al-Kahf.
rows.anchor: روى ابن إسحاق أن قريشا بعثوا النضر بن الحارث ، وعقبة بن أبي معيط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three-question account raises a chronology problem because the spirit answer appears here in al-Isra, revealed before al-Kahf; perhaps the spirit was asked separately first, or this verse was inserted into the surah later.
rows.anchor: ويدفع الإشكال أنه يجوز أن يكون السؤال عن الروح وقع منفردا أول مرة

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority hold that all these passages were revealed in Mecca; al-Tabari transmits from ʿAta ibn Yasar that the statement about receiving little knowledge was revealed there.
rows.anchor: والجمهور على أن الجميع نزل بمكة ، قال الطبري عن عطاء بن يسار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrator says this account makes the insertion’s place depend on the verse having been revealed between the surrounding passages.
rows.anchor: وبذلك يكون موقع هذه الآية بين الآيات التي قبلها والتي بعدها مسببا

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reports that Jews asked the Prophet about the spirit in Medina; he paused until revelation came, then recited this verse.
rows.anchor: وأما ما روي في ( صحيح البخاري ) عن ابن مسعود أنه قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reconciles Ibn Masud’s Medina report with Ibn Abbas’s Quraysh report by proposing that the question first came from Quraysh and later from Jews; the Prophet expected the Jews to understand better, but the same answer was repeated or ordered again.
rows.anchor: فالجمع بينه وبين حديث ابن عباس المتقدم : أن اليهود لما سألوا النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers that historical accounts conflated matters: Quraysh drew questions from both Jews and Christians, while the Cave and Dhul-Qarnayn accounts had Christian associations, leaving the spirit question from Jews.
rows.anchor: والذي يترجح عندي : أن فيما ذكره أهل السير تخليطا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Questioning may recur in different settings, as people with limited knowledge repeat their few questions at each gathering.
rows.anchor: على أنه يجوز أن يتكرر السؤال في مناسبات وذلك شأن الذين معارفهم محدودة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question seeks the nature of what Arabic calls the spirit, whose general presence is intuitively known.
rows.anchor: وسؤالهم عن الروح معناه أنهم سألوا عن بيان ماهية ما يعبر عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One sense of spirit is the hidden entity diffused through the human body, inferred from perception and thought, which enters the fetus after 120 days; it is also called the soul.
rows.anchor: والروح : يطلق على الموجود الخفي المنتشر في سائر الجسد الإنساني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This spirit is the one mentioned in the account of God breathing His spirit into the human, and the same entity may be called النفس.
rows.anchor: وهذا الإطلاق هو الذي في قوله تعالى : { فإذا سويته ونفخت فيه من روحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On one analysis من is partitive and أمر means divine command or affair, as in the description of revelation as a spirit from God’s command.
rows.anchor: و ( من ) للتبعيض ، فيكون هذا الإطلاق كقوله : { وكذلك أوحينا إليك روحا من أمرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If أمر is the creative command, من can mark origin: the spirit proceeds from God’s act of creation, as in His command “Be.”
rows.anchor: وتكون ( من ) ابتدائية كما في قوله : إنما قولنا لشيء إذا أردناه أن نقول له كن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, أمر is a verbal noun used for its object and من is partitive; روح then means Gabriel, one of God’s creatures commanded to convey revelation.
rows.anchor: أو يراد بالمصدر معنى المفعول مثل الخلق و ( من ) تبعيضية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi transmits from Ibn Wahb that Malik said no answer came to the Prophet on this question.
rows.anchor: وروى ابن العربي في الأحكام عن ابن وهب عن مالك أنه قال : لم يأته في ذلك جواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is not a direct account of the spirit’s nature but redirects the inquiry and tells the questioners that this knowledge was withheld; all the possibilities are intended as a comprehensive, genus-level definition.
rows.anchor: أي أن قوله : قل الروح من أمر ربي } ليس جوابا ببيان ما سألوا عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement about little knowledge may address Quraysh or their Jewish informants, serve as a general concluding comment, or address Muslims; “little” is relative to all knowable facts and God’s knowledge.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن تكون مما أمر الله رسوله أن يقوله للسائلين

rows.speaker: اليهود
rows.claim: A Tirmidhi report says the Jews claimed they possessed much knowledge through the Torah; the verse in the Cave chapter was then revealed about the inexhaustibility of God’s words.
rows.anchor: وفي ( جامع الترمذي ) قالوا ( أي اليهود ) : ( أوتينا علما كثيرا

rows.speaker: عطاء بن يسار
rows.claim: Al-Tabari transmits from Ata that the little-knowledge verse was Meccan; when Jewish scholars later challenged its scope, the Prophet answered that it addressed both them and his own people.
rows.anchor: وأوضح من هذا ما رواه الطبري عن عطاء بن يسار قال : نزلت بمكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report continues that the Prophet said Torah knowledge is little relative to God’s knowledge, though acting on what they received could benefit them; a verse in Luqman was then revealed.
rows.anchor: هي في علم الله قليل ، وقد آتاكم ما إن عملتم به انتفعتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning follows the Quran’s healing and mercy: knowledge should prompt gratitude, not conceit, since God can withdraw it; this cautions the Prophet and, by extension, other scholars.
rows.anchor: أعقب ذلك بالتنبيه إلى الشكر على نعمة العلم دفعا لغرور النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement explicitly warns of removal but indirectly expresses favor, as the next verse explains; the Prophet is addressed because his knowledge is greatest.
rows.anchor: فالكلام صريحه تحذير ، وهو كناية عن الامتنان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām introduces an unspoken oath, and the emphatic future verb answers that oath and thereby supplies the conditional answer.
rows.anchor: واللام موطئة للقسم المحذوف قبل الشرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath response also supplies the conditional answer, so no separate conditional response is needed.
rows.anchor: وهو دليل جواب الشرط ومغن عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ثم orders the denial of any recovery by rhetorical rank, since inability to regain the lost revelation is more grievous than losing it.
rows.anchor: و ( ثم ) للترتيب الرتبي ، لأن نفي الطمع في استرجاع المسلوب أشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وكيل is one entrusted with a task; here it means defender, intercessor, or advocate able to secure restoration of the revelation.
rows.anchor: والوكيل : من يوكل إليه المهم . والمراد به هنا المدافع عنك والشفيع لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وكيل is used here for an advocate seeking restoration of a withdrawn favor, whereas نصير in the preceding warning concerns defending against punishment or avenging its recipient.
rows.anchor: وذكر هنا { وكيلا } وفي الآية قبلها { نصيرا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إلا رحمة من ربك is a disconnected exception functioning as a qualification: divine mercy in fact prevented the hypothetical removal of revelation.
rows.anchor: والاستثناء في قوله : { إلا رحمة من ربك } منقطع فحرف الاستثناء فيه بمعنى الاستدراك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage hints at the Qur'an’s preservation, as affirmed in the verse that says God guards the Reminder.
rows.anchor: وهذا إيماء إلى بقاء القرآن وحفظه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following clause explains why mercy prevented removal: God’s favor to the Prophet was great; كان and the emphatic particle reinforce the explanation.
rows.anchor: وموقع إن فضله كان عليك كبيرا } موقع التعليل للاستثناء المنقطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge begins a further statement of favor and explains the preceding claim of great favor; it honors the Qur'an for believers and challenges those who reject it.
rows.anchor: استئناف للزيادة في الامتنان . وهو استئناف بياني لمضمون جملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām introduces an oath; the response omits the usual lām to avoid placing two lām particles together, and the conditional response is supplied by the oath response.
rows.anchor: وجرد الجواب من اللام الغالب اقترانها بجواب القسم كراهية اجتماع لامين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gathering of humans and jinn means united judgment and intent, not merely cooperative effort; even if they actively aided one another, they could not produce a likeness.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الاجتماع : الاتفاق واتحاد الرأي ، أي لو تواردت عقول الإنس والجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jinn are included for comprehensiveness and because the challengers believed they could perform extraordinary acts.
rows.anchor: وذكر الجن مع الإنس لقصد التعميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A likeness to the Qur'an would have to match its combined eloquence, rhetoric, meanings, ethics, and laws, the domains of its verbal and intellectual inimitability.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالمماثلة للقرآن : المماثلة في مجموع الفصاحة والبلاغة والمعاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final concessive clause stresses that the imagined cooperation would not help; ظهير means helper, and the comparison makes the united effort especially explicit.
rows.anchor: والظهير : المعين . والمعنى : ولو تعاون الإنس والجن على أن يأتوا بمثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After challenging eloquent opponents, God cites the Qur'an’s virtues and censures their refusal to benefit from its many parables; مثل may also mean any good state worthy of illustration.
rows.anchor: لما تحدى الله بلغاء المشركين بالإعجاز تطاول عليهم بذكر فضائل القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is coordinated with the Qur'anic challenge and shares its function of expressing favor and disabling opponents; oath and verification particles rebut their claim that it is not from God.
rows.anchor: فجملة ولقد صرفنا } معطوفة على جملة { قل لئن اجتمعت الإنس والجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike the earlier mention of Qur'anic variety used to rebuke the polytheists, للناس addresses all people because this passage presents the challenge to believers and unbelievers alike.
rows.anchor: وزيد في هذه الآية قيد للناس } دون الآية السابقة لأن هذه الآية واردة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People is placed before Qur'an because the audience is central to this challenge; a new rhetorical priority may precede what is intrinsically more central because that is already familiar.
rows.anchor: ووجه تقديم أحد المتعلقين بفعل { صرفنا } على الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite الناس is best understood generally, as confirmed by the statement that most people refused except in disbelief.
rows.anchor: والأظهر كون التعريف في { الناس } للعموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Specifying that the Qur'an contains every kind of parable heightens the challenge: eloquence in one subject does not ensure ability in another, and they could not match even part of it.
rows.anchor: فإن كثرة أغراض الكلام أشد تعجيزا لمن يروم معارضته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من is partitive while كل gives comprehensive scope; the Qur'an contains portions from every kind of elevated parable, with the noun’s indefinite form magnifying its honor.
rows.anchor: فالقرآن مشتمل على أبعاض من جميع أنواع المثل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted object of أبى is action upon the Qur'an, supplied by context.
rows.anchor: وحذف مفعول { أبى } للقرينة ، أي أبى العمل به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception in إلا كفورا appears to exclude a narrower form of refusal but reinforces it, since rejection is more specific than the omitted object; it is an empty exception licensed by أبى’s negative sense.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله : { إلا كفورا } تأكيد الشيء بما يشبه ضده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كفور means one who denies and obstinately rejects the Qur'an’s guidance.
rows.anchor: والكفور بضم الكاف المجحود ، أي جحدوا بما في القرآن من هدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demands follow the refusal of the Qur'an: some of the rejecters made these proposals, but the plural does not mean every opponent recited every demand; at least some addressed Muhammad directly.
rows.anchor: عطف جملة { وقالوا } على جملة { فأبى أكثر الناس إلا كفورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq recounts that named Quraysh leaders summoned the Prophet after sunset, criticized him, offered wealth or status, then escalated to demands for signs when he stood firm.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر ابن إسحاق : أن عتبة بن ربيعة ، وشيبة بن ربيعة ، وأبا سفيان بن حرب

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي أمية المخزومي
rows.claim: He is reported as the one who asked the Prophet to ascend to heaven and bring down a book.
rows.anchor: وروي أن الذي سأل ما حكي بقوله تعالى : أو ترقى في السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their use of لن reflects their stated insistence that they would never believe; the land is Mecca, definite by reference, whose scarcity of water makes the spring request apt.
rows.anchor: وحكى الله امتناعم عن الإيمان بحرف ( لن ) لمفيد للتأييد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تفجير is an intensified splitting open, like light cleaving darkness at dawn; the intensive form suits a spring and rivers, as in the cited cave and garden verses.
rows.anchor: والتفجير : مصدر فجر بالتشديد مبالغة في الفجر

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read تفجر with the tāʾ and geminated jīm, from the intensive verb فجر.
rows.anchor: وقرأه الجمهور بضم التاء وتشديد الجيم على أنه مضارع ( فجر ) المضاعف

rows.speaker: عاصم، حمزة، الكسائي، خلف
rows.claim: These readers use the simpler verb فجر; the spring itself indicates the intended result, so the reading need not imply intensification.
rows.anchor: وقرأه عاصم ، وحمزة ، والكسائي ، وخلف بفتح التاء وسكون الفاء وضم الجيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لن نؤمن لك means they will not affirm that he is God’s messenger; إيمان here means belief or assent and is commonly construed with لام as a clarifying, emphatic object marker.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { لن نؤمن لك } لن نصدقك أنك رسول الله إلينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām after آمن may also distinguish believing someone from making someone secure; Ibn Hisham’s treatment of the marker overlooks this and similar examples.
rows.anchor: وقد يقال : إنها لدفع التباس مفعول فعل ( آمن ) بمعنى صدق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ينبوع denotes a copious, unfailing spring; its يفعول pattern is an irregular intensive form, and lexicalists catalogued the Arabic words of this pattern.
rows.anchor: والينبوع : اسم للعين الكثيرة النبع التي لا ينضب ماؤها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden, palms, grapes, and rivers repeat imagery used in the parable of the garden in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: والجنة ، والنخيل ، والعنب ، والأنهار تقدمت في قوله :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They specify a garden belonging to the Prophet to show, rhetorically, that they would accept a benefit for him rather than seek it for themselves: either a public spring or a private garden crossed by streams.
rows.anchor: وخصوا هذه الجنة بأن تكون له ، لأن شأن الجنة أن تكون خاصة لملك واحد معين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The absolute object تفجيرا indicates numerous channels: the verb already conveys intensive splitting, so the added object signals multiplication suited to streams branching through a garden.
rows.anchor: وذكر المفعول المطلق بقوله : { تفجيرا } للدلالة على التكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All readers geminate فتفجر here, unlike the earlier verb; the reading preserves a subtle numerical implication and is one of the Qur'an’s forms of inimitability.
rows.anchor: ويدل لهذا المعنى إجماع القراء على قراءة { فتفجر } هنا بالتشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demand shifts from beneficial marvels to harmful ones, theatrically widening the challenge: let the Prophet produce a sign even if it harms them.
rows.anchor: انتقال من تحديه بخوارق فيها منافع لهم إلى تحديه بخوارق فيها مضرتهم

rows.speaker: نافع، ابن عامر، أبو بكر عن عاصم، أبو جعفر
rows.claim: These readers vocalize كسفا with a fatḥa on the sīn, the plural of كسفة, a fragment or piece.
rows.anchor: وكذلك قرأه نافع ، وابن عامر ، وأبو بكر عن عاصم ، وأبو جعفر

rows.speaker: باقون
rows.claim: The other readers use a still sīn, understanding the word as a passive description meaning cut off.
rows.anchor: وقرأه الباقون بسكون السين بمعنى المفعول ، أي المكسوف بمعنى المقطوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: زعم is speech regarded as unlikely or impossible; قبيل is a group of one kind, here an unknown special company of angels; زخرف means gold.
rows.anchor: والزعم : القول المستبعد أو المحال . والقبيل : الجماعة من جنس واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using في with ascent to heaven depicts a staged ascent, like climbing a ladder.
rows.anchor: وإنما عدي { ترقى في السماء } بحرف ( في ) الظرفية للإشارة إلى أن الرقي تدرج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their book demand would require a complete text descending at once as proof he reached heaven; they wrongly infer from gradual revelation that it reflects human deliberation and fabrication.
rows.anchor: ولعلهم إنما أرادوا أن ينزل عليهم من السماء كتابا كاملا دفعة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is said that ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Umayya asked for a book accompanied by four angels who would testify for the Prophet.
rows.anchor: قيل : قائل ذلك عبد الله بن أبي أمية ، قال : حتى تأتينا بكتاب معه أربعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in لرقيك may clarify that ascent is the object they refuse to believe, or mark its cause with the object of believe omitted; either reading expresses mockery and denial of their own eyes without a book.
rows.anchor: واللام في قوله : { لرقيك } يجوز أن تكون لام التبيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سبحان ربي expresses astonishment, followed by a rhetorical denial and restrictive statement: the Prophet is only a human messenger, not a creator who controls what they demand.
rows.anchor: أمره الله بأن يجيبهم بما يدل على التعجب من كلامهم بكلمة { سبحان ربي }

none: verse text only; the segment ends before any commentary
